result:
Cities have secret conversations. Brick by brick, their windows whisper to one another while streets carry the day’s rumors to every corner. Beneath the ordinary rhythm of footsteps and engines lies another city, visible only to those willing to notice it.

I love maps that admit uncertainty. A neat blue line may suggest certainty, yet every journey bends around weather, mood, hunger, and chance. The most honest map perhaps leaves blank spaces marked “you are here,” reminding us that location is temporary and human.

On rainy afternoons, I imagine old shops opening onto alternate histories. A cobbler repairs not only shoes but famous lost soles. A bookseller keeps books that were never written, carefully dusted and waiting for the right reader. A baker sells bread containing memories, so each slice tastes differently depending on the morning it was baked.

Perhaps imagination is simply attention without embarrassment. It lets a broken chair become a throne, a stranger’s smile become a small festival, and an empty afternoon become a doorway. We do not need extraordinary circumstances to cross that doorway; we only need to pause long enough to see the invitation.

Even familiar places change when we change. A park bench holds another story, a puddle reflects another sky, and the same bus stop becomes briefly ours. Life rarely asks permission before becoming strange, yet most of us spend so much time explaining it that we forget to take part.

I try to leave a little room each day for wonder, always.
